title: Tag-document linking
content_html:
Tag-document linking

Prerequisites

Tag Vocabulary Import Retirement removes bulk registry and alias import before this feature extends the per-tag schema. It is a separate Roadmap feature and must complete before the document association delivery changes registry records.

Manage Sub-Scope Documents must complete before the one-off migration. Creating a large document set is not a useful outcome while Docs Viewer management cannot navigate, view, and source-edit that set coherently.

tags are defined in tag registry studio/data/canonical/tags/tag-registry.json and may also have associated documentation in docs-viewer/scopes/analysis/source/sub-scopes/tags/documents.

the documentation is not intended to be kept in sync with the summary information in the tag registry, nor be deleted when a tag is deleted from the registry.

the following is however needed:

  • a one-off process to create a document for each existing tag whose registry record does not already contain an explicit document ID.
  • the document link recorded in the tag registry record, and editable in the Studio tag registry modal for a tag.
  • a way of linking from a tag in /studio/tag-registry/ to the document in /docs/?scope=analysis...

One-off migration contract

The migration is driven only by tag registry records and their explicit document-ID field. For each tag without that field, it allocates a new immutable doc_id, creates one document in the Analysis tags sub-scope, and writes that new ID back to the tag record.

Each new document starts with:

---
doc_id: <allocated immutable document ID>
title: "<tag label>"
added_date: <migration timestamp>
last_updated: <migration date>
parent_id: ""
group: "<tag group>"
viewable: true
---
# <tag label>

<tag registry description>

The registry description is copied once as the initial paragraph. It is seed content, not a synchronization contract.

The migration explicitly chooses viewable: true because the tag documents are intended to be public. This is an outcome choice, not a technical limitation: the migration could author viewable: false, and either value could later be changed directly in source. This feature does not add a visibility control.

Migration remains blocked until the management prerequisite is complete. External source editing is available, but it is not a substitute for a usable Docs Viewer workflow for the resulting document set.

The three documents already in the tags sub-scope are not inspected, matched, reused, moved, or updated by the migration. Their unique doc_id values remain their identities. Unless a registry record is linked to one separately through an explicit document ID, they remain independent documents and do not reduce the migration's create set.

Neither title nor title + group is ever used for reconciliation. group exists only to support filtering, visible group presentation, and styling in the Tags report.

Tag edit modal contract

The existing Tag Registry edit modal is the initial association and navigation surface.

  • It exposes one optional editable document-ID field.
  • Save persists the exact ID, or clears it when empty, through the ordinary tag edit mutation. It does not update the document.
  • The field accepts immutable Docs Viewer doc_id values for the Analysis tags sub-scope.
  • Open derives /docs/?scope=analysis&doc=d-20260624-213316-478639&subdoc=<document ID>; the URL is not stored in the registry.
  • Open is available only when the current field value resolves to a listed Analysis tags document. Empty or unresolved values show a contained unavailable state and do not render a dead link.
  • The modal can set, change, clear, save, and open an association. It does not create, import, edit, or delete sub-scope documents.

Related Docs Viewer workflow

Dense sub-scope navigation and Markdown source editing belong to Manage Sub-Scope Documents, not this feature. That feature is a prerequisite for the migration. Tag-document linking then owns the public document creation, registry association, and public deep link.

Downstream semantic-token dependency

A Tag semantic-token target cannot be registered until it can resolve to a stable, workable destination. The registry doc_id association and public subdoc URL produced by this feature provide that destination.

Tag token work therefore waits for this feature and its prerequisites. It must not resolve tags by mutable label or title + group, and it must not add placeholder target-lookup rows without a usable href.

there is also currently a structural problem: the registry recognises that tags are in groups, and a tag label can be in multiple groups. this is why tag_id is a concatination of group and label. the current sub-scope documents do not recognise this structure. documents can be listed in /docs/?scope=analysis&doc=d-20260624-213316-478639 but cannot be filtered (or styled) by group. To do this, we would need an additional front-matter field 'group'.

Current schema

tag-registry:

{
  "tag_id": "subject:bird",
  "group": "subject",
  "label": "bird",
  "description": "Depicted bird: an observable element the viewer can point to. Useful for content-level linking across media; keep separate from domain framing and theme inference to reduce ambiguity.",
  "updated_at_utc": "2026-03-03T17:43:04Z"
}
